questions: No additional substantive reading is sufficiently supported to add as a distinct predicate. Could the contextual emphasis on business support cumulative requirements? A conjunction is compatible with a necessary minimum, but the supplied text does not establish that all three factors are required or sufficient.
What relevant requirements appear in the referenced Circular and Ordinance? Their missing provisions prevent resolution of the sufficiency dispute.

Does “such services” merely identify the services being supplied, or incorporate their regulated status into the business factor? Likewise, does “the business” require hong_kong to imply business? These dependencies require clarification without assigning unknown inputs.

The prior selected-factor proposal identifies no textual selection mechanism or specified factor-specific conditions. What source language would support that interpretation beyond ordinary inclusive disjunction?

secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.

readings.distinction: The first defensible interpretation gives inclusive disjunction scope over the enumerated factors and treats that minimum as sufficient for the selected antecedent. It duplicates the existing disjunctive proposals rather than adding diversity. Its connective analysis is direct, but its sufficiency assumption is less secure than the necessary-minimum reading.

vocabulary_concerns: The three facts express inclusive disjunction and conjunction, but cannot identify unspecified additional requirements. Encoding the necessary minimum as the complete trigger would add a sufficiency assumption.
The business fact compresses case-dependent classification, ordinary-course treatment and possible exceptions. Their separate effects cannot be tested with this vocabulary.
The hong_kong fact refers to “That business”; its treatment when business is false or unknown is unspecified. Neither independence nor a default false value is justified.
The regulated fact absorbs carve-outs whose boundaries and incorporated authority cannot be independently examined here.

Licensing consequences and licence possession are outside the supplied facts. This is consistent with the bounded antecedent experiment, but prevents treating its result as a complete licensing verdict.

A missing selector is not itself evidence of a plausible selected-factor reading. Ordinary existential satisfaction across three factors is already expressible by disjunction; additional factor-specific conditions need textual support.
